canonical_statement: For a positive finite spatial dimension, positive constant density and heat capacity, nonnegative constant isotropic conductivity, a temperature field, heat-flux field, and volumetric source: if q = -k grad T and rho*c*T_t = -div q + Q pointwise, then rho*c*T_t = k*Delta T + Q pointwise.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat with 0 < n; spatial points Space n = Fin n -> Real; time and scalar coefficients in Real; proposition in Prop
ordered_binders: heatFlux : Real -> Space n -> Space n
forall t x, heatFlux t x = fun i => -conductivity * gradient (temperature t) x i
rho * heatCapacity * timeDerivative temperature t x = -divergence (heatFlux t) x + source t x
conclusion: rho * heatCapacity * timeDerivative temperature t x = conductivity * laplacian (temperature t) x + source t x

operator_conventions.gradient: coordinate evaluation of the Frechet derivative on Pi.single i 1

statement_selection: The intake requires a conditional heat-equation derivation rather than treating the empirical constitutive law as a proved universal fact. The selected elementary homogeneous isotropic classical form keeps the energy balance as an independent hypothesis and includes a volumetric source. Anisotropic, variable-coefficient, weak, boundary-value, and source-free forms are not silently substituted.
